news.title: India vs Brazil: The Football Friendly No One Needs
news.lede: India are set to host Brazil this Saturday, October 3rd, in the first international break since the World Cup. It will be the first meeting between the two men’s national teams, in what the All India Football Federation (AIFF) has described as “a landmark chapter in the history of Indian football.” Given the overwhelming support for the Seleção and its massive fanbase in India, you might expect unanimous excitement for this unprecedented friendly. That, however, has not been the case.

news.title: 'Give me my Club World Cup!' - Former Fluminense star Felipe Melo wants 2023 title handed to him after Man City found guilty of FFP breaches
news.lede: The former Fluminense defensive midfielder jokingly demanded that the 2023 Club World Cup trophy be handed over to him following City's guilty verdict for financial rule breaches . Speaking at the Ole Summit 2026 in Buenos Aires, the veteran known as the Pitbull brought up his side's comprehensive 4-0 defeat in the showpiece fixture in Saudi Arabia . He seized upon the prospect of the Citizens being stripped of their silverware to take aim at European football's overwhelming financial hegemony.' %Reports of severe sanctions looming over the English heavyweights triggered a light-hearted response on social media from the former player after his panel appearance.

news.title: Sports - Portugal: Ronaldo walks away
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal’s training camp after several days of tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus. Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença travelled to Copenhagen to try to ease the situation, without success. Ronaldo eventually missed training and left Denmark on his private jet. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner must now explain his decision.

news.title: 'A cancer on football' - Football Leaks whistleblower Rui Pinto launches sensational attack on FIFA president Gianni Infantino over Man City and PSG FFP allegations
news.lede: The man behind the Football Leaks revelations has launched a blistering attack on FIFA president Gianni Infantino, claiming the Swiss official has no place in the sport’s future. Rui Pinto, whose leaked documents sparked the long-running Premier League investigation into Manchester City, alleges that Infantino actively helped elite clubs circumvent financial regulations during his time at UEFA. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-year period, a verdict stemming directly from data Pinto shared with the public in 2018. While the club's guilt has been determined, the case remains ongoing as sanctions have not yet been decided, and the Etihad outfit have until October 2 to lodge an appeal against the ruling.

news.title: All Whites take on Panama
news.lede: The All Whites have taken another step forward. They are through to the final of the Kirin Cup, advancing via a penalty shootout over Panama on Thursday night in Yokohama. The match finished 1-1 after 90 minutes, before the New Zealand team were impeccable from the spot, while goalkeeper Alex Paulsen made a critical save for the eventual 5-3 scoreline. It completed a satisfying afternoon for the world No 86 All Whites, who acquitted themselves well against the higher ranked Central American team (44).

news.title: Live: All Whites v Panama Kirin Cup football in Japan
news.lede: The All Whites have advanced to the Kirin Cup final in Japan after beating Panama in a penalty shootout in Yokohama. New Zealand were first on the scorecard when Marko Stamenić found the back of the net after 13 minutes. They looked set to head to the break with a 1-0 lead when Giovany Herbert scored an equaliser for Panama just on halftime. The second half saw a host of personnel changes and neither team really found their rhythm.

news.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola warning fired as Real Madrid circle World Cup star
news.lede: The current lengthy international break has given Liverpool a chance to reflect on the season so far. The summer saw the Reds undergo a bout of surgery on their squad, which has led to a solid, if unspectacular, unbeaten start to the new campaign. One of the areas addressed was the Reds’ attack. Andoni Iraola's star signing in the final third was Bradley Barcola, who joined from Paris Saint-Germain for £123 million.
